name: Cabinet and closet installer (finish carpentry)

google_prefill.phone: [G] the listed phone (stays the business's; customers use Rosie's one number)

A.flow: A: the customer comes to the business (video or phone count as A)

services.name: Design session
services.story: Design session, $35 at the studio; a card saved for the $20 missed-session fee; paid at the studio desk.

services.name: Virtual design session
services.story: Virtual design session, $55, paid in full when booking; credited toward a project if Alex signs.

services.name: Door and drawer front refresh
services.story: Door and drawer front refresh priced from Alex's photos at $90, OK'd by Sam; a card saved; paid at the studio desk.

services.name: Custom wall unit design
services.story: Custom wall unit design, priced at the studio after a $25 consult; a card saved; paid at the desk.

B.flow: B: the business goes to the customer

services.name: Design and measure visit
services.story: Walk-in closet: the $89 design and measure visit, a card saved for the late-cancel fee; Gabe's written quote; the agreement, a $1,600 deposit, a $400 change order; the last $2,000 on the bill Rosie texts.

services.name: Design and measure visit
services.story: The same closet, but Sam bills the deposit and the last payment the business's own way; Rosie sends nothing about money.

services.name: Closet shelf and rod install
services.story: Closet shelf and rod install, $179 from the list; a card saved for the $89 fee; Rosie texts the bill after.

services.name: Cabinet hardware swap
services.story: Cabinet hardware swap, $150, paid in full when booking.

services.name: Pantry shelving build
services.story: Pantry shelving priced from photos at $640 (over $500, so Sam OKs it); a signed agreement; a 25% deposit of $160; the rest on the bill.

questions_before_times: What do you want: a closet system, cabinets, shelving or a small fix?
Which room, and about how big is the space?
A house, an apartment or a business space?
When would you like it done?
safety_stop: a gas smell, sparking or smoking wires, a carbon monoxide alarm
water running inside a wall, or a ceiling sagging
a shelf, cabinet or tall piece that has tipped or fallen on someone
license: if: finish carpentry (cabinets, closets, shelving) needs a contractor license above the state's job-size limit; below it, only a business registration. All of it comes from the state's form.
